claim: Creating an EBS-backed AMI makes snapshots of the instance's root volume and its other attached EBS volumes, and you are charged for those snapshots until you deregister the AMI and delete the snapshots.
question: What does an EBS-backed AMI store its volumes in, and how long are you charged for them?

values.display: creates snapshots of your instance's root volume
charged for the snapshots until you deregister

evidence.quote: During the AMI-creation process, Amazon EC2 creates snapshots of your instance's root volume and any other EBS volumes attached to your instance. You're charged for the snapshots until you deregister the AMI and delete the snapshots.

claim: By default, deregistering an AMI has no effect on the snapshots created with it, which keep incurring storage costs; you can optionally delete the associated snapshots during deregistration, except a snapshot that other AMIs also use.
question: Does deregistering an EBS-backed AMI delete its snapshots?

values.display: also has no effect on any snapshots
optionally delete its associated snapshots
it won't be deleted even if specified

qualifiers.condition: snapshot deletion can be requested at deregistration

evidence.quote: By default, deregistering an AMI also has no effect on any snapshots that were created during the AMI creation process.

When deregistering an AMI, you can optionally delete its associated snapshots at the same time. However, if a snapshot is associated with multiple AMIs, it won't be deleted even if specified for deletion, although the AMI will still be deregistered. Any snapshots not deleted will continue to incur storage costs.

claim: When an instance hibernates, its instance store volumes stay attached but the data on them is lost.
question: What happens to instance store data when an instance hibernates?

values.display: remain attached to the instance
data on the instance store volumes is lost

qualifiers.scope: instance store volumes on a hibernated instance

evidence.quote: Any Amazon EC2 instance store volumes remain attached to the instance, but the data on the instance store volumes is lost.

claim: On an instance with an instance store root volume, data persists while the instance runs but is deleted when the instance terminates or fails; such instances do not support Stop and cannot be restored after they fail or terminate.
question: What happens to an instance with an instance store root volume when it fails or terminates?

values.display: deleted when the instance is terminated
do not support the Stop action
it can't be restored

qualifiers.scope: instances with an instance store root volume

evidence.quote: Any data on the instance store volumes persists as long as the instance is running, but this data is deleted when the instance is terminated (instances with an instance store root volume do not support the Stop action) or if it fails (such as if an underlying drive has issues).
After an instance with an instance store root volume fails or terminates, it can't be restored.

claim: Only a few older instance types (C1, C3, D2, I2, M1, M2, M3, R3 and X1) support an instance store root volume, and Windows instances do not support instance store root volumes.
question: Which instances can boot from an instance store root volume?

values.display: C1, C3, D2, I2, M1, M2, M3, R3, and X1
do not support instance store root volumes

evidence.quote: Only the following instance types support an instance store volume as the root volume: C1, C3, D2, I2, M1, M2, M3, R3, and X1.
Windows instances do not support instance store root volumes.

claim: When you change the instance type, the instance gets the instance store volumes of the new type (if it supports instance store), but the data does not transfer to the new instance.
question: Does instance store data survive a change of instance type?

values.display: the data does not transfer to the new instance
supported by the new instance type

evidence.quote: If the new instance type supports instance store, the instance gets the number of instance store volumes supported by the new instance type, but the data does not transfer to the new instance.

claim: Instance store data is not included in an EBS-backed AMI created from the instance, nor on the instance store volumes of instances launched from that AMI.
question: Does creating an EBS-backed AMI capture the data on instance store volumes?

values.display: not included in the EBS-backed AMI
instances launched from that AMI

qualifiers.scope: instance store volumes, EBS-backed AMI creation

evidence.quote: The data is not included in the EBS-backed AMI, and it is not included on instance store volumes attached to instances launched from that AMI.

claim: On some instance store volumes the first write to each location is slower than later writes, so AWS recommends initializing the drives for high disk performance; instance types with direct-attached SSD and TRIM support give maximum performance at launch without initialization.
question: Do instance store volumes need initialization for best performance?

values.display: performs more slowly than subsequent writes
maximum performance at launch time, without initialization

qualifiers.condition: not needed on SSD instance store with TRIM support

evidence.quote: Because of the way that Amazon EC2 virtualizes disks, the first write to any location on some instance store volumes performs more slowly than subsequent writes.
Instance types with direct-attached solid state drives (SSD) and TRIM support provide maximum performance at launch time, without initialization.

claim: An instance store provides temporary block-level storage on disks that are physically attached to the host computer, exposed to the instance as one or more block devices.
question: Where does instance store storage physically live?

values.display: temporary block-level storage
physically attached to the host computer

evidence.quote: An instance store provides temporary block-level storage for your EC2 instance. This storage is provided by disks that are physically attached to the host computer.
An instance store consists of one or more instance store volumes exposed as block devices.

claim: EBS volumes provide benefits that instance store volumes do not provide.
question: Why choose EBS over instance store?

values.display: benefits that are not provided by instance store volumes
not provided by instance store volumes

evidence.quote: EBS volumes provide benefits that are not provided by instance store volumes.
